q3.story: A skipper who checks the tide before choosing a time scrolls to the table: Sat 17 Oct afternoon HW is '14:32', captioned 'times in UTC', and the gate is open 'about two hours before high water until two hours after'. The Arrival time list does not say what zone its times are in. The persona does not know whether the harbour works in local time or UTC (it is listed in their does-not-know), and in mid-October UK clocks are an hour ahead of UTC. They have to work out on their own whether 15:00 means 14:00 UTC or 15:00 UTC against a 14:32 UTC high water, and the arrival they pick may land an hour away from where they think it sits in the gate window. Missing knowledge: which clock the arrival times use, and the high-water and gate times in that same clock.
evidence: aria/root/default/375-light.yml: table 'High water at the quay, times in UTC', cell '14:32'; combobox 'Arrival time' options without zone

steps.failure_story: The tide table gives high water in UTC while the arrival-time list gives no zone; the persona, unsure which clock the harbour uses, must convert by hand to check whether their 15:00 arrival falls inside the sill-gate window. For this date 15:00 falls inside the window either way, so they can probably go on, but only after working it out themselves and without being sure.

steps.visible_cues: Four radio cards: 'Pontoon A, berth 6 - Boats up to 8 metres... £2.80 per metre per night', 'Pontoon B, berth 14 - Boats up to 10 metres... £3.20', 'Pontoon C, berth 3 - Boats up to 12 metres... £3.60', 'Wall berth 2 - Boats up to 15 metres. Settles on soft mud at low water. £2.40'. No statement of which length the limits refer to.
steps.most_likely_action: Either Pontoon C, berth 3 (if they read the limit as length overall) or Pontoon B, berth 14 (if they read it as hull length, 9.6 m, which fits under 10 m and is cheaper).

q1.story: They have to pick a berth to continue; the heading asks them to.

q2.story: Pontoon C, berth 3 is the third card; its title is partly visible at the bottom of the first screen and fully visible after a short scroll.

q3.story: The persona knows two lengths for their boat: 10.4 m overall including the bowsprit and 9.6 m hull. Each card says only 'Boats up to N metres'. The persona does not know which pontoon is long enough (it is listed in their does-not-know), and the page does not say whether the limit is length overall or hull length. Reading it as hull length, Pontoon B, berth 14 ('up to 10 metres', and cheaper at £3.20 than £3.60) looks right. Missing knowledge: which length the berth limits are measured against. Probed consequence: choosing B14 and later entering 10.4 ends on 'Booking stopped. This booking cannot continue. Reference BK-409.' with no reason and no way back (probes/14). Entering 9.6 instead goes through to a B14 booking summary 'Curlew, 9.6 metres long' (probes/7), so the boat is booked into a berth shorter than its overall length.
evidence: aria/berths-html-date-2026-10-17-nights-2-arrive-15-00/default/375-light.yml: radio 'Pontoon B, berth 14 Boats up to 10 metres...'

steps.failure_story: A skipper who reads 'Boats up to 10 metres' as hull length picks the cheaper Pontoon B, berth 14. If they later enter their overall length, the booking dead-ends on 'Booking stopped' with only a reference code: no reason, no route back to choose another berth. If they enter hull length, they end up booked into a berth too short for the boat overall. Either way they are unlikely to reach the right berth without phoning the office. Missing knowledge: what length the limits refer to.

notes: Four-question (full) variant at 375 x 812, light. Isolated subagent walk. The correct sequence replayed cleanly (probes/5, all 19 actions ok, no console or network errors); this is not a prediction that users succeed, since the walker knew the path. The goto action is the start state and is not counted as a step. To evidence the step-5 failure story I also probed the persona's most likely wrong choice (B14 with hull length 9.6: probes/7; B14 with LOA 10.4: probes/14); these are evidence probes, not an alternative path. The journey file's _comment mentions a ground-truth file; I did not look for or read it. Not raised as candidates: the confirmation omits the arrival time and gate window; the boat page does not repeat the chosen berth; the tide table sits below the Check berths button at 375 px. All three are minor and are noted in the step stories.
